details.description: True structuring: 5 unrelated senders, no prior relationship, deposit $8,200-$9,600 into a newly-created collector within a 6-hour window
True structuring: single originator makes 4 rapid same-day transfers to a new beneficiary, each in the $9,000-$9,700 range, within 3 hours
True structuring: 6 unrelated senders deposit tightly clustered $9,000-$9,900 amounts into a collector within 12 hours
True structuring: 4 senders deposit oddly-specific (non-round) amounts avoiding the threshold, within 8 hours
True structuring: 5 senders converge on a collector across two consecutive days (structuring split across days to look less like a single-day burst)
Decoy: legitimate payroll run, one employer fanning OUT to 6 named employee accounts with varying role-based salary amounts, same payday
Decoy: recurring monthly vendor/rent payments from one business to 3 fixed vendors, spread across a full month, not a single burst
Decoy: SaaS subscription billing, fan-in from 8 distinct unrelated customers paying a fixed low recurring fee, well below any reporting threshold
Decoy: seasonal retail sales spike, fan-in from 8 genuine unrelated retail customers over a 5-day holiday sale window, naturally varying amounts
Hard decoy: one customer's own two accounts transfer $9,800 each on the same day into a shared family account, explained by a bank per-transaction limit, not evasion
Hard decoy: 3 distinct unrelated corporate clients pay similar-magnitude legitimate invoices within 2 days, purely because that is the going rate for the service
